objective.statement: Name the white keys A to G using the groups of black keys.
successCriteria: I can say the seven letter names in order, and I know they start again after G.
I can find C and F by looking at the black keys.
I can name any white key on the keyboard.

explanation.text: Music uses just seven letter names: A, B, C, D, E, F and G. After G they start again at A, one step higher.
On a piano the black keys come in groups of two and groups of three. Those groups are your map for finding the white keys.

music.textAlternative: A piano keyboard with the white key C highlighted, just to the left of a group of two black keys.

explanation.caption: C is the white key just to the left of a group of two black keys.

music.textAlternative: A piano keyboard with seven white keys highlighted and named C, D, E, F, G, A and B.

explanation.caption: From C the white keys run C D E F G A B, and then C comes round again.

explanation.text: Put your finger on C and say the letters as you move right. Moving right sounds higher; moving left sounds lower.

music.textAlternative: Eight white keys from C up to the next C.

steps: Find the group of two black keys. The white key just to its left is C. Tap it to hear it.
Tap each white key to the right in turn: D, E, F, G, A, B. Listen to the sound climbing.
Now find the group of three black keys. The white key just to its left is F.
After B the pattern repeats: the next white key is C again, one octave higher.
demonstration.textAlternative: A keyboard of eight white keys from C to the next C. Each key can be tapped to hear its note, and its letter name is spoken in the step list.
